column11: lookup.py demand Adakveo: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $26,003,300.29 over 419 beneficiaries = $62,060 per beneficiary
column12: Judgement on the comparator. Adakveo is the marketed branded SCD drug labelled to reduce the frequency of VOCs, and VOC reduction is a co-primary endpoint of HIBISCUS. Part B is its main channel (419 beneficiaries against 85 in Part D, where the figure is $58,308). No oral SCD comparator can replace it under the house rule: lookup.py demand returns nothing for Oxbryta, Endari, Siklos, Droxia, Hydrea or hydroxyurea, and book.db drug_demand has no row for Oxbryta's asset (id 1315) although the osivelotor seed cites one ($66,631 per Part D beneficiary in 2023). Published list prices exist but none is a like-for-like marketed anchor: Oxbryta's WAC was $10,417 a month, $125,004 a year (GBT FY2021 10-K, as the osivelotor seed quotes it), but Pfizer withdrew it in September 2024; Endari, the one marketed branded oral, costs about $24,000 a year (ICER 2021, via search), a glutamine powder with a weak effect and not a price for a new molecule. The net price here, $58,548, lands within 3% of Oxbryta's measured net on the osivelotor seed ($66,631 less its filed 14.5% = $56,990), so pricing an oral off an infused Part B product does not move the net. The case against: Adakveo is a monthly IV antibody and etavopivat a daily oral in Part D; Adakveo's confirmatory Phase 3 STAND was negative (Abboud MR et al., Lancet Haematol 2025;12(4):e248-e257, PMID 40088922: VOC rate ratio 1.08 at 5 mg/kg and 0.89 at 7.5 mg/kg against placebo). The case for a much higher price: mitapivat, the first PKR activator, is priced at a WAC of about $425,000 a year as Aqvesme in thalassaemia (Xtalks, Fintool via search, not opened), and its SCD sNDA has a Priority Review PDUFA date of 2026-11-01 under accelerated approval (Agios release, investor.agios.com, via search). Once Agios sets an SCD price, a same-class oral in the same patients with a published list price is the better anchor and this row should be re-seeded. SCD's large, mostly Medicaid population argues against an orphan-level price. In DKK because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $62,060.00 at DKK/USD 0.152643 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) is DKK 406,568.87
